name: Taldyk Pass
near: Ak-Bosogo — about 6 km as the crow flies (OSM marker, catalogue calculation). The nearest base villages on the highway: Sopu-Korgon (north side, before the serpentine) and Sary-Tash (south side, ~20 km beyond the pass); Gulcha, the district centre, is ~80 km to the north. Road distances of the approaches are not confirmed.
elev: 3,615 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, the pass sign in travellers’ photos); other sources round it to 3,600 m (too.kg, economist.kg) or give 3,588 m (Nomad's Land). Nearby on the same highway is the “40 Years of Kyrgyzstan” pass, 3,541 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan).
short: Taldyk is a year-round drivable road pass (about 3,600 m) in the Alay range on the Osh — Sary-Tash highway, the gateway to the Alay valley and the Pamir Highway.
desc: The Taldyk Pass in the Alay range links the Gulcha river valley (the Fergana side) with the Alay valley. The Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam (China) and Osh — Sary-Tash — Kyzyl-Art (Tajikistan, Pamir Highway, M41) highways run over it; the pass lies at about km 163 of the Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam international corridor (economist.kg, 2026). The first wheeled road was built in the late 19th century, the modern highway in the 1930s–40s; at the pass stands a monument to the construction engineer Yu. Grushko (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The northern slope is a famous serpentine, the southern one a gentle descent to Sary-Tash. The road is paved and considered passable all year, but in winter the section at km 161–179 is avalanche-prone; construction of a ~3.2 km tunnel is planned to start in 2027 (economist.kg, 08.2026).
guide: Taldyk is the moment when the green of Fergana stays below and the Alay valley and the wall of the Trans-Alay range with Lenin Peak (7,134 m) open up ahead. Stop at the top by the monument to engineer Grushko, who built this road in the 1930s–40s — from here is the best view of the northern slope’s serpentine. On a single drive from Osh you can easily pass through “all four seasons” here: heat below, snow possibly lying at the top, so a warm jacket is needed even in July. The pass is a transit point: plan it as a photo stop on the way to Sary-Tash, Sary-Mogol or the Pamirs, and spend the night in the Alay valley. In winter watch for Emergency Ministry (MChS) warnings — the section at km 161–179 is avalanche-prone.
see: The northern-slope serpentine with a view of the Gulcha valley; the monument to engineer Yu. Grushko on the saddle; the pass sign with its elevation; views of the Alay valley and the Trans-Alay range (Lenin Peak 7,134 m — in clear weather); the neighbouring “40 Years of Kyrgyzstan” pass (3,541 m). Red cliffs and a change of landscape from forest-steppe to high-mountain tundra along the road.
skip: You are not continuing into the Alay valley, the Pamirs or China — driving 3+ hours one way from Osh specially for the pass makes little sense. You tolerate altitude and serpentines badly. In winter — if you have no winter tyres and no experience of driving on mountain roads.
diff: Easy to visit: it is a stop by a paved highway, no hiking climb. The load comes from the altitude of ~3,600 m (mild altitude sickness is possible with a fast climb from Osh, ~1,000 m) and the serpentine of the northern slope (editorial; too.kg).
when: June — September: the road is dry, views are open. The pass is officially passable all year (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan), but from November to March avalanches, drifts and black ice are possible — the Emergency Ministry (MChS) issues warnings for the km 161–179 section (Kaktus, 15.11.2024).
hours: Around the clock; it is a section of a state highway with no checkpoint. Temporary traffic restrictions are possible during snowfall and avalanche danger (Kaktus, 2024).
daytime: Morning — less cloud over the Alay valley and a better chance of seeing Lenin Peak; public transport from Osh leaves around 14:00, so by marshrutka (minibus) you pass the pass towards evening (nomadasaurus, 2026). Avoid the serpentine in the dark (editorial).
how: From Osh south along the Osh — Gulcha — Sary-Tash highway (M41 / EM-05): about 160 km to the pass (too.kg), about 3 hours by car; the Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka takes about 3 h (nomadasaurus, 2026). The tunnel fee on the Bishkek — Osh highway (50/200 som) does not apply to this route.
needcar: Yes. The pass is a point on the highway; you need your own/rented car, a taxi or a seat in a marshrutka/shared taxi Osh — Sary-Tash (Daroot-Korgon). On a marshrutka the driver does not always stop for photos — for a photo stop a taxi or your own car is more convenient (editorial).
self: Yes: the road is paved, there are signs, no guide is needed; a border-zone permit is not required for the Osh — Sary-Tash highway itself (permit requirements apply to the Lenin Peak area and other zones — tour.too.kg). In winter — only with a good forecast and winter tyres.
roadtype: Paved mountain highway M41 / Osh — Sary-Tash — Irkeshtam; the northern slope is a steep serpentine, the southern one gentle (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). Rockfalls, road subsidence and slope movements have been recorded on the section (Ministry of Transport, 2021, via economist.kg 2026). A ~3.2 km tunnel is planned (work to start in 2027).
traveltime: From Osh — about 3 h by car to the pass (~160 km, too.kg; editorial on the marshrutka time to Sary-Tash ~3 h, nomadasaurus 2026). From the pass to Sary-Tash — ~20–30 min (editorial).
stay: There is no accommodation at the pass. The nearest overnights are guesthouses in Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol; in Sary-Mogol: Tilek Guesthouse, Peak Lenin Guesthouse, Guesthouse Hamza — about $15 per person with breakfast, CBT Sary Mogol — $20 (nomadasaurus, 2026). Specific guesthouses in Sary-Tash were not checked.
net: Not confirmed for the pass saddle. Sary-Mogol has 4G (nomadasaurus 2026 writes “Megafon” — probably MegaCom). According to general reviews Beeline works best in the mountains (bestofosh). No reports on coverage specifically at Taldyk were found.
entry: Free: it is a section of a state highway, no source mentions a fee for crossing the pass (tunnel fees apply on the Bishkek — Osh highway, not here).
transfer: Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka ~350 som per person; Osh — Daroot-Korgon 300 som (marshrutka) / 400 som (shared taxi) (nomadasaurus, 2026); shared taxi $8–10 per person (eurasia.travel, 12.2024); private taxi Osh — Irkeshtam 4,500 som per car (2019, outdated).
bring: A warm jacket and hat even in summer (at the pass ~3,600 m it is sharply colder than in Osh); sunglasses and sunscreen; water and a snack (no shops at the pass — editorial). In winter — winter tyres, chains, a fuel reserve; keep 500 m between cars in avalanche periods (Emergency Ministry (MChS) recommendation, Kaktus 2024).
warn: Altitude about 3,600 m — headache and shortness of breath are possible with a fast climb. In winter and spring (November — March) — avalanches, snow drifts, black ice on the km 161–179 section; the Emergency Ministry (MChS) recommends winter tyres and a 500 m distance (Kaktus, 15.11.2024). Rockfalls and road subsidence are recorded on the section (economist.kg, 2026). In the coming years tunnel construction (start 2027) and related traffic restrictions are possible.
food: Not confirmed: no sources list any eateries at the pass itself. You can eat in the villages along the highway (Gulcha, Sary-Tash) and in the guesthouses of Sary-Mogol — it is recommended to have dinner at the guesthouse (nomadasaurus, 2026); specific cafes near the pass were not checked.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 38 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, per catalogue check). Typical pros from travel notes: views of the serpentine and the Alay valley, a change of seasons in one trip, good asphalt. Cons: cold and wind at the top, winter avalanches. No separate listing for the pass was found on TripAdvisor or 2GIS.
p.sum: Taldyk is a photo stop on the paved Osh — Sary-Tash highway (M41), about 160 km and ~3 h from Osh. It is easiest to drive it in your own car or by taxi/transfer with a stop at the top; the Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka (350 som, until 14:00) does not always stop for photos. Spend the night in Sary-Tash (~20 km beyond the pass) or Sary-Mogol, not on the saddle. In winter (November — March) watch for Emergency Ministry (MChS) warnings for the km 161–179 section.
p.apps.0.title: From the north: from Osh via Gulcha (serpentine)
p.apps.0.route: Osh → Langar → Gulcha (district centre) → Sopu-Korgon → northern-slope serpentine → Taldyk saddle
p.apps.0.surface: Paved all the way (M41 / EM-05), the northern slope is a steep serpentine; rockfalls and road subsidence
p.apps.0.season: Year-round; November — March the avalanche-prone km 161–179 section, black ice, drifts. In summer mudflows occur: on 24.06.2026 a mudflow blocked the km 58–200 section for ~1.5–2 h
p.apps.0.last: The last big choice of fuel stations/ATMs is Osh; Gulcha has shops and cafes (district centre). Coverage along the highway is patchy, not confirmed on the saddle
p.apps.0.parking.d: Roadside/area by the monument to engineer Yu. Grushko and the pass sign on the saddle; free, unguarded
p.apps.0.trail.d: No hiking route — a stop by the road
p.apps.0.haz: Avalanches and black ice in winter, mudflows after downpours in summer, rockfalls, altitude ~3,600 m

p.apps.1.last: Sary-Tash: one ATM (may not work), dollars exchanged at the fuel station, small shops, cafe Akun (wikivoyage, 2019–2025)

p.onsite.other.0.details: The Yu. Grushko monument, the 3,615 m sign, a view of the northern-slope serpentine; in clear weather from the south side — the Trans-Alay range and Lenin Peak
p.onsite.camping: Not customary on the saddle itself (wind, cold); cyclists camp by the Taldyk river below the pass (cycleblaze, 2016) and in the Alay valley.
p.onsite.photo_spots: The top of the serpentine by the monument — a view down onto the loops of the road; from the southern descent — a panorama of the Alay valley and the Trans-Alay range. The best light is in the morning.

p.iti.0.title: Osh → Alay transit in a day
p.iti.0.plan: 08:00 leave Osh → 10:00 Gulcha (coffee/fuel) → 11:00 Taldyk, 20–30 min photo stop → 11:30 Sary-Tash → 12:30 Sary-Mogol, in the evening Tulpar-Kol.
p.iti.1.title: 2–3 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Osh — Taldyk — Sary-Mogol (overnight, acclimatisation). Day 2: Tulpar-Kol and Achyk-Tash. Day 3: back to Osh or on to the Pamirs via Kyzyl-Art (Tajikistan, a visa/GBAO permit is needed).
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: It makes sense to combine with Sary-Mogol, Tulpar-Kol and Achyk-Tash (along one highway). Kojokelen is through another valley (from Osh to the west) and cannot be combined into one car route.
p.season: June — September: dry road, best views. October — snow is possible on the saddle. November — March: avalanche danger and black ice at km 161–179, the Emergency Ministry (MChS) advises winter tyres and a 500 m distance. April — May: thaw, rockfalls. In summer — short mudflows after downpours (June 2026).
p.budget.economy: Osh — Sary-Tash marshrutka 350 som + a guesthouse in Sary-Tash ~$20 (≈1,750 som) with dinner and breakfast ≈ 2,100 som per person.
p.budget.comfort: A 4×4 transfer Osh — Alay $300 per car (≈26,000 som, shared by 3–4) + a guesthouse/camp $15–85
p.permits: Not required: it is a section of a state highway, no fee. A border-zone permit is needed further on — for the Lenin Peak area (Achyk-Tash) and for the trip to Kyzyl-Art.
p.access: Suitable for everyone, including children and older people: a viewpoint by the road. Limitations — the altitude of ~3,600 m (fast climb from Osh, ~1,000 m) and cold/wind. Stroller — only by the car, the area is uneven.
